title: New Residential Construction (Building Permits, Housing Starts, Completions — October 2026 data) — 8:30 a.m. ET, the corridor's only SOLO housing-starts nowcast vintage of Q4 and the last edition before the funding cliff
source: CENSUS: three independent census.gov primaries fetched direct 2026-09-06 by this event's own initial research, plus one non-Census corroboration. (1) economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html (HTTP 200, 91,396 bytes, 179 table rows parsed), row "New Residential Construction (Building Permits, Housing Starts, and Housing Completions) | November 18, 2026 | 8:30 AM | October 2026", release code A202611180830, reference A202610 — and the page's only four `Suspended` rows are Preliminary Steel Imports and the Advance Economic Indicators Report, not this series. (2) construction/soc/schedule.html, the Survey of Construction Release Schedule (HTTP 200, 59,625 bytes), whose October-2026 row reads "October 2026 | November 18, 2026 | November 25, 2026" under the column heads "(12th Workday) New Residential Construction - 8:30 a.m." and "(17th Workday) Revised Building Permits - 8:00 a.m. / New Residential Sales - 10:00 a.m.". (3) census.gov/construction/xls/historic_release_dates.xls (HTTP 200, 55,808 bytes, 515 rows 1984-01 → 2026-11), whose 2026-10 reference row reads NRC 2026-11-18, NRS 2026-11-25. (4) The Atlanta Fed's GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx PostedUpdates sheet (HTTP 200, 16,944 bytes), whose 2026-11-18 08:30 row reads "Housing starts" ALONE. Promoted `estimate` → `confirmed` and `EST:` → `CENSUS:` on the two-primary precedent this calendar already carries for durable-goods-2026-11-25, m3-full-report-2026-12-03 and the sibling housing-starts-2026-12-17. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: Canonical file written by this id's own initial research (2026-09-06) after reading the one proposal that created it, `from-existing-home-sales-2026-11-12`, now shadowed. Three findings answer what that proposal left open. (1) THE OPEN QUESTION IS ANSWERED AND THE HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED: the proposal asked whether a 14:00 FOMC MINUTES release compresses the morning the way a 14:00 SEP decision does. It does not. On 721 SPY sessions of hourly bars (2023-10-09 → 2026-09-04), decision days crush every morning hour — the 09:30 hour takes 31.4% of session range vs 53.1% baseline, the 10:30 hour 26.3% vs 40.2% (independently reproducing the 12-09 ledger's 26.0%/40.4%), 11:30 20.0% vs 33.6%, 12:30 19.8% vs 32.0%, all p<0.005 — then the 14:30 hour explodes to 74.8% vs 28.9% and the session runs WIDER (1.13% vs 0.85%, p=0.03). Minutes days share none of it: every morning hour sits at baseline (09:30 53.4% vs 53.1%, p=0.96; 10:30 44.8/40.2 p=0.29; 11:30 30.9/33.6 p=0.47; 12:30 29.8/32.0 p=0.53), the session range is unchanged (0.81% vs 0.85%, p=0.73), and only the 14:30 hour lifts modestly (40.9% vs 28.9%) — about a quarter of a decision day's move. At daily resolution the 19 historical housing-starts days that also carried FOMC minutes are indistinguishable from starts days that did not (ITB gap 0.562% vs 0.576%, p=0.94; SPY range 1.137% vs 1.059%, p=0.68). The practical consequence: the fomc-minutes-2026-11-18 co-release does NOT disqualify this session as a clean instance of the sibling's homebuilder kill switch. (2) THIS IS THE SOLO VINTAGE 12-17 IS NOT. The Atlanta Fed schedules the 2026-11-18 08:30 GDPNow vintage as "Housing starts" alone, where 12-17 reads "Housing starts, Import and export prices" — October import/export prices publish 11-17 instead. Re-measured this session from ContribArchives (1,871 vintages 2014-05-01 → 2026-07-28 = 1,822 same-quarter deltas, matching the sibling exactly): on the 93 solo starts vintages residential investment is the LARGEST of the eight component moves 95.7% of the time against a 20.7% base rate, vs 5 of 10 on the shared starts+import/export pairing the 12-17 lane measured. So the corridor's readable residential nowcast is here, not on 12-17. (3) NO CLIFF EXPOSURE, AND THAT IS THE ASYMMETRY. cr-expiry-2026-12-11 is 23 days AFTER this print; the sibling's finding that all 9 of this series' 514 out-of-month slips since 1984 are funding-lapse slips therefore does not reach 11-18 at all. If the cliff bites, the 2025-26 precedent (114 dark days, eight months to normal cadence) makes this October edition the last residential-construction datapoint anyone reads until roughly Q1-2027. Impact LOW and symbols empty are re-derived here, not inherited: ITB's overnight gap on Census's own 515 release dates reproduces the sibling era-for-era (2006-09 1.104%/0.766% p=0.034; 2010-15 0.615%/0.401% p=0.002; 2016-20 0.381%/0.339% p=0.50; 2021-26 0.575%/0.487% p=0.21), and starts-only days show no intraday signature at any hour (every p ≥ 0.41). Unlike 12-17 there is no opex confound — 11-18 is opex-week Wednesday (T-2), measured null for ITB (gap 0.374% vs 0.401%, p=0.50; November-only 0.267% vs 0.399%, p=0.36) — where 12-17 is December opex EVE (p=0.021). The session is loaded anyway: 08:30 this print, 10:00 NAR's October Pending Home Sales Index (verified on NAR's own 2026 schedule), 14:00 the FOMC minutes, with APEC leaders in Shenzhen the same day. October is not a distinctive reference month (HOUST median |m/m| 5.70% vs 6.35% for other months, p=0.69). Date `confirmed`; nothing here licenses an entry.
